subject: Placeholder environment block textures for the subway, mutant railway, monorail and doomsday door levels: rail track, platform edge and arches, station tiles, tunnel mouth, train window, door and bogie, pillars, bench, rubble, water, pipe bundle, monorail beam, wooden crate, quay drain, vault door hub and plate, mine cart, cracked ledge.
visual_approach: Programmer pixel art: hard edges, no antialiasing, grimy concrete, rusty steel and dark water with 1 px highlight / shade bevels and dark seams; red stripes, amber hazard bands and green glows; colours from the project's shared palette.

generation_settings.palette: 85 hex constants: the 41 of tools/blocks_placeholder.py followed by 44 in tools/blocks_themes/common.py, all from the project's shared palette (not in the repository)

creative_seed.note: No generator seed. The script uses random.Random with fixed seeds (per-call seeds in the helpers, 301-336 in this theme's tiles) for small details such as rust, grime, ballast stones, rubble chunks and water glints. Every rebuild is identical.

style_inheritance: follows blocks-placeholder.png (same tile size, bevel and seam rules, palette extended from its palette)

post_analysis.provenance: Post-generation subagent visual analysis; not part of the original generation prompt.
post_analysis.subject: A 7 x 3 grid of 21 pixel-art 64 px tiles for a ruined subway / railway theme: track, platform, station wall, tunnel, train parts, pillars, bench, rubble, water, pipes, beam, crate, drain, vault door, plate, mine cart and ledge.
post_analysis.composition: Tiles sit edge to edge with no gaps or labels. Each tile is a separate side-on (2D) view, not one continuous scene. Rows are 7, 7 and 7 tiles. Tiles with a dark navy background (pillars, bench, rubble, water, pipes, cart, ledge) have empty space around the object.
post_analysis.environment: Abandoned underground transit: platform, tunnel, rolling stock, flooded track and a sealed vault door. Wet, rusty and derelict feel.
post_analysis.colors: Dominant dark slate / navy and mid greys, with rust orange-brown streaks and pipes, amber-and-black hazard stripes, red stripes on train parts and a pillar, teal water and small teal glints, a single yellow-green glow (tunnel, vault slit), cream and lavender-grey wall bricks.
post_analysis.materials: Looks like grimy painted steel with rivets, rough concrete, glazed ceramic tile, rusted pipe, weathered wood planks, dark murky water, loose rock and perforated metal. Thin vertical rust streaks overlay most tiles.
post_analysis.lighting: Flat, unlit pixel-art shading with a light top edge and darker lower edge on some forms. No cast shadows. The only emissive elements are the green glow in the tunnel and the green slit in the vault hub. Roughly consistent across tiles.
standout_features: Tunnel arch with a glowing green light and converging rails at the far end
Large vault door hub with eight spokes and a green light slit
Consistent rust-streak overlay unifying all tiles
Amber hazard stripes on pillar and vault plate
Mine cart loaded with rock on a rail
important_details: Row 1 tile 1 (rail-track): dark band above, a grey rail with four brown sleepers, dark ballast below with small cyan puddle glints - recognisable
Row 1 tile 2 (platform-edge): yellow line and dotted tactile strip at top over a grey grimy concrete face with seams - recognisable
Row 1 tile 3 (platform-arch): grey beam at top, arched dark recess with a rust pipe cross and rubble at the base - recognisable
Row 1 tile 4 (station-tile-wall): offset rows of grey, lavender and cream glazed tiles with rust streaks and a few dark chips - recognisable
Row 1 tile 5 (tunnel-arch): grey stone arch ring, dark interior, yellow-green glow with a rail converging at the bottom - recognisable
Row 1 tile 6 (train-window): grey carriage panel with a large dark rounded window, red stripe, rivet rows below - recognisable
Row 1 tile 7 (train-door): two grey door leaves with small rounded windows, red stripe across and a small plaque - recognisable
Row 2 tile 1 (train-bogie): dark undercarriage with two round wheels with brown axle boxes on a rail strip - recognisable as wheels; reads more as machinery than a bogie
Row 2 tile 2 (concrete-pillar): lavender-grey column with a red band near the bottom on a dark background, rust streaks - recognisable
Row 2 tile 3 (pillar-hazard): grey steel column with an amber-and-black hazard band at the bottom and rivets - recognisable
Row 2 tile 4 (bench): grey perforated seat and back panels with a dark leg frame on a grey wall panel - recognisable
Row 2 tile 5 (rubble): pile of dark and grey broken chunks with brown bent bars - recognisable as debris; shapes are jumbled
Row 2 tile 6 (water-surface): dark teal water with a lighter top line, amber dashes and horizontal ripple streaks - recognisable
Row 2 tile 7 (pipe-bundle): horizontal rust, grey and teal pipes with flanges, vertical dark brackets - recognisable
Row 3 tile 1 (monorail-beam): grey concrete beam with a rail on top, seam, dark murky band below with faint hangers - recognisable as a beam; the underside is hard to read
Row 3 tile 2 (wood-crate): brown planks with diagonal brace and grey corner plates - recognisable
Row 3 tile 3 (quay-drain): grey wall with a recessed barred opening in rust bars, a small cyan trickle below - recognisable
Row 3 tile 4 (vault-door-hub): concentric grey and brown rings with a yellow-green slit and eight brown spokes - recognisable
Row 3 tile 5 (vault-door-plate): four riveted grey plates with a diagonal amber-and-black stripe crossing them - recognisable
Row 3 tile 6 (mine-cart): brown ore cart with ribs, rock pile on top, two small wheels on a rail line - recognisable
Row 3 tile 7 (cracked-ledge): grey cracked slab on top with a jagged underside and teal drips on dark navy - recognisable
post_analysis.synopsis: A coherent set of 21 flat pixel-art tiles for a derelict subway level. Palette, outline weight and rust overlay are consistent. All tiles read as their names. Tiles are separate side views, so there is no shared perspective to check.

findings.issue: Rubble tile shapes are jumbled; individual chunks and bent bars are hard to separate
Underside of the beam is dark and murky; hangers and drips are hard to see, so it reads partly as a platform base or water
Train-bogie reads as two round machines with brown boxes more than as a bogie with a frame

defect_analysis.overall: No obvious structural, perspective, floating-object or lighting defect is seen. Only minor readability issues listed above.

mismatches_or_uncertainties: Vault-door-hub spokes extend past the tile edge by design; seamless joining to neighbouring tiles was not checked.
Tiling behaviour (seams) was not checked visually; only single tiles are visible.
Rust streaks look the same across unrelated tiles, so they read as a global overlay rather than per-object wear.
